status: DESIGN ONLY - not executed, not approved for execution. Separately versioned from the frozen primary 6.

excluded_candidate.reason: Deterministic diversity rule (2 THREE_WAY + 1 TWO_WAY by ascending composition-tuple sort) selects only 1 of the 2 qualifying TWO_WAY candidates; this one sorts second within its class and was not selected. Not excluded for any coverage-outcome reason.

selection_rule_reproducibility: select_diverse_three(candidates, n_three_way=2, n_two_way=1): sort all qualifying candidates by composition tuple ascending; partition by discrimination_class; take the first n_three_way THREE_WAY and first n_two_way TWO_WAY items. Fully mechanical - takes no coverage counts, no Jev output, and no outcome preference as input. Reproducible by anyone given only the candidate list and the two integer parameters.
selection_rule_robustness_check: the alternative allocation (1 THREE_WAY + 2 TWO_WAY) was also tested and independently clears the >=6 sufficiency threshold on all 3 pairs (see console output) - the specific 2:1 ratio was not necessary for the result, evidence against the rule having been reverse-engineered to hit the target.
selection_criteria: A defined under the existing round-half-up rule
selected by exhaustive search + a pre-registered diversity rule (2 THREE_WAY + 1 TWO_WAY, sorted deterministically) - not by inspecting any Jev response, since none exists

sentence_count_metadata.flagged_confound: Composition-level pairwise separation (the mathematical M/X/A relationship) is unaffected by sentence count and has been verified independently of it. However, input LENGTH itself is a separate variable this supplement introduces: whether Jev's actual aggregation behavior differs between 4-sentence and 5-sentence inputs is untested and unrelated to which severity levels are present. Any eventual results report must keep three things separate: (1) composition-level pairwise separation [verified, this document], (2) input-length effects [NOT tested - no n=5 control exists yet to isolate this], (3) actual Jev semantic evidence [not yet collected]. This is a documented, unresolved limitation, not a claim that n=4 and n=5 items are equivalent.

no_selection_based_on_jev_output: Confirmed structurally: this entire script makes zero API calls and reads no Jev response data; candidate discovery and selection are pure functions of the composition math (mode/max/mean) defined before this document existed.
sufficiency_threshold_rationale: matches the precedent set by X-vs-A's full 6/6 coverage in the original 6-item design - applied symmetrically to all three pairs. This is a MATCHED PRECEDENT, explicitly NOT a validated sufficiency threshold - whether >=6 is scientifically adequate remains open (see score_semantic_identification_protocol.md's decision gate).
decision_gate: Per score_semantic_validation_specification.md §8's three-tier hierarchy: this document addresses verifier/design-level coverage only. Semantic validity (is M/X/A correct?) and research validity (is this design scientifically adequate?) remain OPEN and are not advanced by clearing this numeric threshold.
note: This supplement improves pairwise coverage counts. It does NOT establish that M, X, or A is correct, that these items are representative of real score inputs, that each item has equal evidentiary value, or that meeting this numeric threshold is scientifically sufficient - see score_semantic_validation_specification.md §8's three-tier validity hierarchy, unchanged by this document.
